messages:
kevin: Heads-up — hit a correctness/regression on staging: after the driver roll (build 2026.03.15-rc2) a bunch of KV cache hits returned stale KV entries that were for the previous kernel path. Repro: run long chat with repeated prompts, then deploy driver -> some responses show decode artifacts.
lisa: :eyes: can you paste the minimal repro and which cache keying we currently persist? thinking it's a key-namespace mismatch on driver vs runtime.
kevin: repro steps in a gist: 1) start convo (seqlen 120 avg), 2) send ~500 requests over 15m, 3) deploy driver with kernel selector change (arch-aware mapping), 4) observe ~1.2% token corruptions and some hung responses. Kernel autotuner switched from cuopt-v1 -> cuopt-v2 mid-flight.
ananya: is this the new kernel-path signature (we added arch+quant flags)? if driver hash changed existing keys should've been invalidated. sounds like persistence layer didn't get driver metadata.
ajay: quick dump of the cache key pattern in prod currently: `model:{model_id}:seqlen:{seqlen_bin}:kernel:{kernel_sig}:driver:{driver_id}` — but TTLs differ: driver is not included in persistent key for on-disk lane, only in in-memory index. that was intentional to allow hot-swap but maybe unsafe.
kevin: reproduced with logging. snippet:
```
cache_key = f"{model_id}|{seqlen_bin}|{kernel_sig}"
persist_meta = {"driver_hint": driver_hash}
# persisted entry lacked driver_hash in key, only in meta
```
lisa: that explains it. when driver selector mutates kernel_sig for same model+seqlen, persisted key collision -> loader reuses old KV cache block with mismatched kernel layout. bad.
runtime-bot: deploy event: driver rollout 2026.03.15-rc2 -> canary 10% completed at 1933056900
ananya: perf side note: after driver swap we saw p99 spike +3.7% and throughput -11% on the canary cluster; CPU on CPU-hosted decoders rose noticeably. profiler shows wasted decode cycles due to repeated reserialization error handling.
ajay: proposal A (simpler): include driver_build_id and kernel_descriptor in the persisted key (full key): `model|seqlen|kernel|driver|quant` — but that will blow up persisted footprint when drivers change frequently.
kevin: proposal B: two-tier keying: persistent-key = `model|seqlen|kernel_family` (stable across minor driver tweaks) + persistent version vector; runtime in-memory index adds `driver_hash` and `kernel_variant` for exact match. on load, require persisted.version == runtime.expected_version OR treat as warm cache and rebuild.
lisa: we also need an explicit invalidation hook in the driver rollout flow: when driver changes kernel families we should call the cache-service invalidate API for affected model/seqlen cohorts. add as post-deploy hook in deploy pipeline.
ananya: thoughts on persistence layout: store entry metadata with explicit fields: `model_id`, `seqlen_bin`, `kernel_family`, `kernel_variant`, `driver_hash`, `persist_version`, `created_at`. then loader can reason and skip mismatches. avoid unstructured blobs.
ajay: agreed. also add a fast check at load: if kernel_variant != runtime.expected_layout then drop and mark as cold. that avoids silent corruption.
kevin: perf tradeoffs: rekeying on every driver bump increases cold miss rate and token cost. can we support a compatibility matrix instead? driver declares which previous kernel_variants are binary-compatible for KV blocks.
lisa: yep add `compat_map` to driver manifest: e.g., `cuopt-v2: [cuopt-v1, cuopt-v1-quantized]` — loader uses this to accept persisted entries for cuopt-v2.
ajay: implementation plan:
- short-term (hotfix): include `driver_build_id` in persisted key and flood-invalidate in deployment script for canary rollout (low complexity). rollback window 2h.
- medium-term: metadata-rich persistence + compat_map + two-tier keying + loader strictness.
- metrics: instrument persistent_hit_mismatch, loader_drops, p99_after_invalidate.
ananya: I ran a quick sim with compat_map acceptance and it reduced cold misses by ~60% while preventing the corruption path. sim logs:
```
scenario: 10k entries, driver bump that is compat with 6k entries -> accepted 5.8k, dropped 200 -> cache warm
baseline (blind accept) -> corrupted 120 entries -> decode errors
```
kevin: sounds good. action items assigned:
- ajay: hotfix patch + invalidate script (ETA today EOD) :shipit:
- lisa: update deploy pipeline to call invalidate hook and ensure driver manifest includes compat_map (ETA 2 days)
- ananya: add sim harness and run across common models and seqlen distributions (ETA 48h)
- runtime-bot: run canary after hotfix and report metrics to #eng-runtime (automated)
sre-bot: I've added a runbook entry for 'cache-driver-mismatch' with steps: flush cohort, downgrade driver, mass-invalidate. link: https://internal/runbooks/cache-driver-mismatch
lisa: one more: we should include a small checksum for kv-layout in the persisted metadata so cross-process detection is cheap. add `kv_layout_sig`.
ajay: good call.
kevin: ok let's land hotfix, schedule medium-term design in next runtime sprint. will follow up with PR and bench numbers. thanks team :pray:
lisa: thanks — keep alerts in #incidents if anything noisy during canary.
kevin: closing thread, will post PR link when ready."
